t_advice_summary_textbox.text: The gnones will appear in 1 of 4 pairs each is a differeht colout, such as purple and blue, green and orange, etc, each of the gnones in the pair will go to a different forest, a dark forest with a yellow basket, and light forest with a red basket.What you have to decipher is which of the forest generates the most amount of mushrooms, and which gnome you pick goes to which forest. Special attention is made in when you have you multipliersThings not to take any notice off is the number of spots on the hats or anything else this is colour specific

vb_textbox.text: To the best of my knowledge I know the followingYou are presented with 1 of 4 set of 4 gnones, Each of the Gnones show a pair of colours, blue and purple, red and yellow, green and pink, orange and brown, the advice given to me was to focus on gnomes which will specifically go to one one of the two different forests. (There is a Dark forest with red basket) (There is a light forest with a yellow basket) in theory one forest will generate a higher number of mushrooms then the other.However there is a counter argument that 2 things that change has an effect on the which forest is chosen,My logic is a follow, - shape - always pick round over coneIf they are both the same shape always pick lighter colours over darker colours, this also comes up with inconsistencies, however I believe there isnt one set rule to this survey but this cave me a result of over 3500So this gives you two options to use or perhaps you use your own but I wish you the best of luck.
